change: Test-only coordinated memo-cache release after four completed independent serial fixtures and at scope boundaries.
unchanged: All rev-19/rev-20 assertions and eighty test/subtest paths
Cache keys and within-fixture same-input model identity
Immutable baseline/source/import data and partial-type registrations
Canonical CI/shard configuration and test timeouts
Profiling flags, memory-profile sampling rate and pressure/swap/load safeguards
conclusions: The measured peak RSS drops from approximately 8.07/7.29 GiB to 1.35/1.16 GiB while every original test case passes.
Post-GC retained heap drops from approximately 3.03/2.78 GiB to 9.53/11.54 MiB, consistent with releasing transient analyzer graphs while retaining small shared import/source data.
The tradeoff is real: observed package time is about 2.4-2.5 times baseline, and cumulative allocation volume about 2.8-2.9 times baseline because less state is retained for reuse.

Background concurrency differs between runs, so the exact wall-time ratio is not a fully controlled causal estimate. The changes and allocation profiles support a memory-versus-recomputation tradeoff, not an unqualified performance win.
Allocated volume is not required physical RAM. RSS is sampled and may count shared pages more than once.
The first implementation cleared every fixture and passed correctness but was much slower; its separate correctness evidence is retained rather than hidden.
Only independent serial rev-19/rev-20 fixtures use this scope. Do not apply it to active/shared models or parallel consumers without a separate ownership design.
Other high-memory groups and the older Mac full suite remain unmeasured with this change.
Full regression CI and review remain pending before maintenance acceptance; no canonical grouping or production behavior changed.
